plan.title: Lung treated vs control DE with confounded batch label
plan.analytical_narrative: 6 treated vs 6 control lung samples, raw salmon gene counts (12000 genes x 12 samples). Batch B1=all controls, B2=all treated: batch is a perfect confound of condition (design matrix would not be full rank with both terms). Per the knowledge-service flag (R-0005), we do NOT fit a batch term and do NOT apply ComBat-seq/removeBatchEffect/SVA-style correction, since any such 'correction' would remove the condition effect along with the batch. Instead we run standard DESeq2 QC -> filter -> normalize -> Wald test -> apeglm shrinkage -> BH/independent filtering, cross-check with edgeR QLF, and label every downstream result explicitly as confounded (batch effect and treatment effect are statistically indistinguishable; observed differences may reflect processing batch, not treatment). Enrichment is restricted to permitted methods for this confounded/small design per knowledge-service check: GO over-representation (clusterProfiler enrichGO with tested-gene universe, rrvgo redundancy reduction) on the significant gene list, plus GSVA per-sample Hallmark scores as a descriptive supplement (no group inference claimed beyond the same confound caveat). All numeric findings are reported as hypothesis-generating, not causal treatment effects, until an unconfounded replicate design is available.
